title: Why I Joined West Capital Lending
description: Today I start as Vice President at West Capital Lending. Here's why I made the move, what my team is building, and what stays the same for clients and agents.
image_alt: A group of colleagues gathered around a table in a team meeting

faq.q: Is Duke Gallo still working with clients?
faq.a: Yes. Duke and his team continue to work with clients and real estate partners, now as part of West Capital Lending. His cell, (949) 688-5959, is unchanged.

faq.q: Can loan officers join Duke's team at West Capital Lending?
faq.a: Yes. Duke is growing his team and welcomes confidential conversations with loan officers. Visit dukegallo.com/join to get in touch.

body_html:
Today is my first day as Vice President at West Capital Lending.

Changing companies is never a small decision in this business. Your team, your agent partners, and your clients all feel it, and they deserve to know why. So here's the honest version: what drew me here, what we're building, and what stays exactly the same.

It starts with leadership

I've learned that the ceiling on any team is set by the people at the top. When I sat down with Danny and Eric, what stood out wasn't a pitch. It was a clear vision for where this industry is going and how a broker shop should show up for loan officers and their clients along the way.

They think in years, not quarters. They invest in their people. And they lead from the front, which is the only kind of leadership I've ever wanted to follow. When I thought about who I wanted my team learning from over the next decade, the answer was easy.

A culture of winners

Every lender talks about culture. At West Capital Lending you can feel it. The mindset is simple: no one sits around blaming the market. Nobody's waiting on the 10-year Treasury to decide whether they're going to have a good month. People focus on what they control, which is serving clients, building relationships, and doing the work.

And when someone wins, everyone wins. Scenarios get shared. Ideas get shared. Wins get celebrated. That kind of environment makes good loan officers great, and it's exactly the room I want my team in.

In this culture, nobody cares about the 10-year. Everyone focuses on what they can control, and everyone wins together.

Room to build something that lasts

The biggest reason I made this move is opportunity, and not just for me. My team deserves a platform built for sustainable growth: the support, technology, lender access, and leadership to keep getting better year after year, in any rate environment.

We joined West Capital Lending as the largest onboarding group, and we're not slowing down. Our goal is to double the team and reach $1 billion in funded volume in 2027. That's an ambitious number, and I wouldn't put it in writing if I didn't believe in the people around me and the platform behind us.

  • For my loan officers: more resources, more mentorship, and a clear path to grow your business.
  • For loan officers thinking about their next move: we're building, and there's room for people who want to be part of it. Here's what joining my team looks like.

What changes for you, and what doesn't

If you're a client, a past client, or a real estate partner, here's the short version: same great service, now backed by the best leadership in the industry.

  • You'll still work with me and the same team you know.
  • You'll still get fast answers, straight talk, and updates without having to ask.
  • Through the broker channel, we can still compare options across many lenders to find the right fit for your situation.
  • My cell is the same: (949) 688-5959.

For agents, nothing about how we partner changes, except that the team behind your buyers' loans just got stronger. I wrote about what agents should expect from a loan officer, and that standard doesn't move.

Thank you

I want to sincerely thank the leadership at E Mortgage Capital, especially Sam, Kook, and Regina, for their support over the past five years. They gave me the opportunity to grow from branch manager to Vice President and to build a team I'm incredibly proud of. I'm grateful for every lesson and every bit of trust along the way.

And to my team: thank you for believing in this next chapter. We did it together, and we're just getting started.

What's next

Over the coming weeks I'll be sharing more about what we're building at West Capital Lending, here on the blog and in a few industry publications. If you're a client or agent partner with questions about a current or upcoming loan, call or text me anytime. And if you're a loan officer who wants to build something that lasts, let's have a confidential conversation.

Here's to the next chapter.

— Duke
